scope.costco_launch_note: Formal launch date not confirmed; earliest captured written review is used as the observed-start marker.

data_quality.target_written_window_note: All written reviews exposed by the three exact Target product pages were loaded and captured.
data_quality.kroger_note: All visible public cards were captured from four exact Kroger pages; undated cards are excluded unless they exactly match a dated first-party record.
data_quality.amazon_note: Amazon was assessed for all six grocery kits; no exact scoped product page was confirmed. Adjacent sauces and Heat & Eat items were excluded.
data_quality.thrive_note: All written reviews returned by the public review endpoint for three exact-UPC grocery kits were captured. Thrive Cash disclosure is preserved row by row.
data_quality.meijer_note: Three native Meijer-origin reviews were captured from the exact Instacart-hosted listing; syndicated Kevin's rows were deduplicated rather than counted again.
data_quality.listing_note: An exact listing without a public review surface is shown as listing coverage, not as zero reviews. A searched-no-exact-page result is also not a zero-review claim.

incentive_disclosure.note: Future-purchase and Thrive Cash badges are treated as disclosed incentives; explicit sponsorship remains a separate field. No sponsorship inference is made where the review does not disclose it.

value_for_money.definition: All-time written reviews that explicitly indicate insufficient protein, insufficient vegetables, inadequate serving size, or negative price/value tension. Reviews may carry more than one category.

rating_snapshots.note: Listing total includes syndicated Kevin's reviews; three native Meijer-origin rows are incremental.

provocations.title: Is the 2.5-serving promise creating an expectation gap?
provocations.evidence: 51 of 277 grocery-kit written reviews contain a precise low-value signal; 23 specifically flag protein quantity.
provocations.implication: Test pack communication and protein-to-vegetable balance before treating the issue as flavor reformulation.

provocations.title: Did the grocery-kit experience weaken as distribution scaled?
provocations.evidence: On the complete first-party history, grocery kits moved from 4.71 (n=7) in the first six months after launch to 2.75 (n=12) in the latest six months.
provocations.implication: Validate the signal against consumer care, lots, promotions, and channel mix; the written-review bases remain small.

provocations.title: Incentive-bearing cohorts must remain visible, not blended away.
provocations.evidence: 165 written reviews carry a disclosed future-purchase or Thrive Cash incentive; source-specific views preserve that context.
provocations.implication: Use owned-site trends for launch-to-now comparison and retailer cohorts for issue discovery; do not treat the combined rating as a like-for-like trend.

provocations.title: Convenience appears to be an equity worth protecting.
provocations.evidence: Convenience language appears in 153 of 331 deduplicated written reviews.
provocations.implication: Any product or pack change should preserve the under-10-minute, low-mess preparation benefit.

provocations.title: Use retailer variance as a learning agenda, not a scorecard.
provocations.evidence: Target and Kroger aggregates are larger than the owned-site feed for several grocery SKUs, but their populations and syndication rules differ.
provocations.implication: Validate channel, price, promotion, and review-origin metadata before comparing retailer averages as if they were controlled cohorts.
